title: Dolan 1994: peak extensor moment, lumbar flexion and passive share during stoop/squat/freestyle lifts
condition: lifting 0, 10, 20 kg from the floor (stoop, squat, freestyle)

quantity.name: peak extensor moment and passive share
quantity.definition: peak lumbar extensor moment (Nm, from EMG calibration), % lumbar flexion at that instant, passive moment I (Nm) and I as % of peak EM; mean +/- SD

source.authors: Dolan P, Mannion AF, Adams MA
source.sample: 149 healthy volunteers (126 women, mostly nurses; 23 men), no severe LBP history

protocol.summary: Lifts of a pen (0 kg), 10 kg and 20 kg weight-lifter's discs; stoop/squat over ~4 s; EMG and Isotrak at 28 Hz.
how_to_simulate: Reproduce the lift posture at peak moment (lumbar flexion % in the data)
Hand load per row (0, 10 or 20 kg disc held in both hands)
Output: L1-S1 extensor moment and its passive part (passive ligament/disc/muscle) vs active part

subject_model.source: Dolan 1994 Table 1 (page image; pdftotext garbled several entries: men height SD 7, ROF SD 7.7, EMmax range 272-640, women ROF range 33.7-74.8)

protocol.notes: EMG: surface electrodes over the left erector spinae belly at T10 and L3 (raw EMG used only inside each subject's own EMG-moment calibration; the passive moment I is the EM-axis intercept). Lumbar flexion from the 3-Space Isotrak (sensors over L1 and S1 spinous processes), expressed as % of the range erect standing -> full toe-touch flexion. Isometric pulls on a floor load cell in a frame (thighs against a crossbar, hips strapped). Regressions: women I = 4.91e-5 F^3 + 0.7573 B - 24.8 (R2 0.321); men I = 7.97e-5 F^3 + 12.9 (R2 0.389), F = % flexion, B = body mass (kg). Eight subjects lifting 'with as much lordosis as possible' still flexed 57.5% (SD 13.9%).
